Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> In a report published on May 29, 2022, Goldman Sachs declared the bull market for battery metals, particularly lithium, was "over for now." The investment bank forecasted a significant drop in lithium prices, citing a surge in supply that would outpace demand growth. Goldman Sachs projected that after averaging around $54,000 a tonne in 2022, lithium prices would plummet to $16,372 a tonne in 2023. The report explained that a rush of investor capital into supply-side projects created a "fundamental mispricing" and an outsized supply response ahead of the actual demand trend. The release of this bearish forecast prompted a significant sell-off in lithium stocks.

metadata.original_text: This time series records lithium CNY T data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2023-08-28 to 2023-09-12. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Piedmont Lithium announced the strategic appointments of two new senior leaders on June 22, 2023, to bolster its global portfolio of projects. James Griffiths was named Senior Vice President of Corporate Development and Treasury, and Kara deBorde joined as Vice President of Risk Management. According to Keith Phillips, President and CEO of Piedmont, these roles are crucial as the company advances towards revenue generation from its joint ownership in the North American Lithium project and continues to develop its assets in Ghana, Tennessee, and North Carolina. <2> E3 LITHIUM LTD. announced the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for its Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) field pilot plant, located east of Olds, Alberta. These KPIs are designed to measure the success of the pilot's operations, which are intended to validate the DLE technology under real-world conditions. The data gathered will inform the design and cost estimations for E3 Lithium's first commercial facility, marking a crucial step towards commercializing its lithium assets. The company stated that the pilot plant was on track to commence operations in the third quarter of 2023. <3> On June 12, 2023, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced over $192 million in new funding to advance battery recycling technology and strengthen the domestic supply chain. [1, 2] This investment, part of the Biden-Harris Administration's Investing in America agenda, is aimed at meeting the rising demand for electric vehicles (EVs) and stationary energy storage. [2, 5] The funding is allocated to three key areas: $125 million for recycling batteries from consumer products, $60 million for a new Advanced Battery R&D Consortium, and $7.4 million to continue the Lithium-ion Battery Recycling Prize. [1] The initiative seeks to develop consumer education programs, improve state and local recycling infrastructure, and foster research into new battery chemistries using more abundant materials to support the goal of EVs making up 50% of new vehicle sales by 2030. [2, 5] <4> On June 2, 2023, American Lithium Corp. released its financial and operating highlights for the fiscal quarter ending February 28, 2023. The update included progress on its projects in the US and Peru. Notably, the announcement detailed advancements at the TLC Lithium Project in Nevada, which saw a significant increase in measured and indicated lithium resources and the completion of a robust maiden Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA). The company also highlighted its recent listing on the Nasdaq Capital Markets in January 2023. <5> Ford Motor Company announced a series of long-term lithium supply agreements with multiple companies on May 22, 2023, to secure raw materials for its electric vehicle production. The agreements are with U.S.-based companies Albemarle, Compass Minerals, and EnergySource Minerals, as well as Canada-based Nemaska Lithium and Chile-based SQM. These partnerships are structured to ensure the lithium is sourced from the U.S. or countries with a U.S. Free Trade Agreement, a key requirement for vehicles to qualify for IRA tax credits. Albemarle will supply over 100,000 metric tons of battery-grade lithium hydroxide from 2026 to 2030. Compass Minerals will provide up to 40% of its phase-one battery-grade lithium carbonate for a five-year term starting in 2025. EnergySource Minerals is set to supply lithium hydroxide from its Project ATLiS in California, expected to be operational in 2025. The agreements are pivotal to Ford's goal of producing two million EVs annually by the end of 2026. <6> EnergySource Minerals (ESM) announced a binding offtake agreement with Ford Motor Company to supply lithium hydroxide for electric vehicle (EV) batteries. The lithium will be sourced from ESM's Project ATLiS facility, located in Imperial Valley, California, which extracts lithium from geothermal brine. This project will utilize ESM's patented ILiAD direct lithium extraction technology platform, which is designed to be more efficient and sustainable than conventional methods. Commercial production at the Project ATLiS facility is anticipated to commence in 2025. <7> The U.S. Interior Department removed a significant obstacle for Lithium Americas Corp.'s Thacker Pass mine in Nevada by completing a court-ordered analysis. [3] A federal judge in February 2023 had largely upheld the mine's approval but required the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) to analyze whether lands planned for waste and tailings storage contained valuable minerals. [2, 3] The department's solicitor subsequently found that evidence of mineralization exists on nearly all of the claims underlying these sites. [3] This finding addresses the key issue raised by the court, allowing the project to proceed. [1, 5] The decision is part of a broader move by the administration to clarify mineral rights under the 1872 Mining Law. [2] <8> Ioneer announced an updated mineral resource estimate for the South Basin of its Rhyolite Ridge Lithium-Boron Project in Nevada, revealing a 168% increase in lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) to 3.4 million tonnes. [2, 4, 9] The total mineral resource of the deposit is now estimated at 360 million tonnes, which also contains 14.1 million tonnes of boric acid equivalent, an 18% increase. [2, 4, 9] This update, with an effective date of March 31, 2023, was conducted by WSP USA Inc. and for the first time includes both high-boron and low-boron lithium mineralisation. [4] The company noted that all mineralized units remain open in three directions, indicating potential for further resource increases. [4] <9> General Motors' venture capital division, GM Ventures, led a $50 million Series B financing round in EnergyX, a company specializing in direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology. [3, 4, 7, 8] Concurrent with the investment, the two companies entered into a strategic agreement to collaboratively develop and commercialize EnergyX's DLE and refinery technology. [3, 8] The partnership is aimed at securing a North American supply of lithium, a critical component for electric vehicle batteries, to support GM's expanding EV production. [3, 6, 8] Under the agreement, GM will have access to competitive lithium offtakes for its exclusive use. [6, 10] This investment is part of GM's broader strategy to control every stage of its battery supply chain in North America, from raw materials to cell production. [3, 8]

[1, 2, 3] The combined share for hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and battery electric light-duty vehicles fell to 18.0% in Q1 2024, down from 18.8% in the fourth quarter of 2023. [1, 3] This decrease was primarily driven by a drop in battery electric vehicle (BEV) sales, which saw their market share decrease from 8.1% in Q4 2023 to 7.0% in Q1 2024. [1, 2, 3] This marked the first quarterly decline in BEV market share since the second quarter of 2020. [1] <2> Albemarle (NYSE: ALB), a leading global lithium producer, announced its first-quarter 2024 results, reporting a significant downturn in earnings due to collapsing lithium prices. The company's net income attributable to shareholders was $2 million, a stark decrease from the previous year. Net sales for the quarter were $1.4 billion, a 47% decline year-over-year from $2.6 billion. This drop was primarily driven by an 89% decrease in pricing within its Energy Storage division, which more than offset a 31% increase in sales volumes as the company ramped up new projects. The groups claim the EIR fails to adequately address and mitigate the project's impacts on air quality, hazardous waste, and water supply. Furthermore, the suit argues that Imperial County did not conduct meaningful consultation with local Indigenous tribes or require specific mitigation measures to protect tribal interests. The legal challenge seeks a review to determine if the EIR complies with state law or needs revision. <5> The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced a conditional commitment for a $2.26 billion loan to Lithium Americas Corp.'s subsidiary, Lithium Nevada Corp., for the Thacker Pass project in Humboldt County, Nevada. This facility is designed to produce an initial 40,000 tonnes per year of battery-grade lithium carbonate, which could support the production of batteries for up to 800,000 electric vehicles annually. The price decline was attributed to concerns of a short-term oversupply, the end of China's subsidies for electric vehicle purchases, and weaker than anticipated global sales of electric vehicles. [3, 10] This event marked the official start of construction for the Lithium Valley Campus. [2, 3] The first stage of the project is a $1.85 billion development expected to produce 25,000 metric tons of battery-grade lithium hydroxide annually, enough to support the production of approximately 415,000 electric vehicles. [2, 4] The total project has a potential resource capacity to produce 1,100MW of renewable power and around 300,000 metric tonnes of lithium products per year. [4] The data, which reflects the national capacity as of October 1, 2023, indicated that the United States could recycle 35,500 tons of battery materials annually. [3, 4] The report also detailed plans for a significant expansion, with facilities expected to add another 76,000 tons of recycling capacity over the next two to four years. [3, 4] <2> A report from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), using data from Wards Intelligence, revealed a decline in the U.S. market share of electric and hybrid vehicles during the first quarter of 2024. [1, 2, 3] The combined share for hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and battery electric light-duty vehicles fell to 18.0% in Q1 2024, down from 18.8% in the fourth quarter of 2023. [1, 3] This decrease was primarily driven by a drop in battery electric vehicle (BEV) sales, which saw their market share decrease from 8.1% in Q4 2023 to 7.0% in Q1 2024. [1, 2, 3] This marked the first quarterly decline in BEV market share since the second quarter of 2020. [1] <3> Albemarle (NYSE: ALB), a leading global lithium producer, announced its first-quarter 2024 results, reporting a significant downturn in earnings due to collapsing lithium prices. The company's net income attributable to shareholders was $2 million, a stark decrease from the previous year. Net sales for the quarter were $1.4 billion, a 47% decline year-over-year from $2.6 billion. This drop was primarily driven by an 89% decrease in pricing within its Energy Storage division, which more than offset a 31% increase in sales volumes as the company ramped up new projects. Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter stood at $291 million, down from $1.5 billion in the same period of the prior year. The company reported an adjusted diluted earnings per share of $0.26. <4> Following an 80% price collapse in 2023, lithium carbonate prices experienced a modest 10% recovery to US$14,859 per tonne in early 2024, as reported by Motley Fool on April 3, 2024. However, this analysis suggested the price increase was not a fundamental market shift. This view is supported by financial institutions like Goldman Sachs, which predicts that a market bottom for lithium prices will not be reached until 2025 due to ongoing imbalances between supply and demand. <5> On March 13, 2024, conservation and environmental justice groups Comité Civico del Valle and Earthworks filed a lawsuit against Imperial County over the approval of Controlled Thermal Resources' (CTR) Hell's Kitchen lithium project at the Salton Sea. The lawsuit alleges that the county violated the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) with a flawed Environmental Impact Report (EIR). The groups claim the EIR fails to adequately address and mitigate the project's impacts on air quality, hazardous waste, and water supply. Furthermore, the suit argues that Imperial County did not conduct meaningful consultation with local Indigenous tribes or require specific mitigation measures to protect tribal interests. The legal challenge seeks a review to determine if the EIR complies with state law or needs revision. <6> The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced a conditional commitment for a $2.26 billion loan to Lithium Americas Corp.'s subsidiary, Lithium Nevada Corp., for the Thacker Pass project in Humboldt County, Nevada. The loan, offered through the Advanced Technology Vehicles Manufacturing (ATVM) Loan Program, is designated for the construction of a processing facility. This facility is designed to produce an initial 40,000 tonnes per year of battery-grade lithium carbonate, which could support the production of batteries for up to 800,000 electric vehicles annually. The project is located at the site of the largest confirmed lithium resource in North America and is expected to create approximately 1,800 construction jobs and 360 operational jobs. This conditional commitment was a significant milestone <7> Sustainable battery materials provider Ascend Elements announced on February 20, 2024, that it had raised an additional $162 million in equity investments. This funding, from investors including Just Climate, Clearvision Ventures, and IRONGREY, brought the company's 12-month fundraising total to $704 million. The capital is intended to accelerate the construction of its Apex 1 manufacturing facility in Hopkinsville, Kentucky. The Apex 1 plant is set to be North America's first sustainable cathode precursor (pCAM) manufacturing facility and is anticipated to begin operations in the first quarter of 2025. Once completed, the one-million-square-foot facility will produce sustainable pCAM and cathode active materials (CAM) for up to 750,000 electric vehicles per year. <8> On February 8, 2024, Goldman Sachs released a forecast, maintaining a bearish outlook on the lithium market due to anticipated oversupply. The investment bank predicted that lithium prices would not bottom out until 2025. The forecast estimated average 2024 prices for lithium carbonate at $13,377 per tonne and lithium hydroxide at $14,263 per tonne. Other reports from Goldman Sachs around the same period featured slightly different but comparable price forecasts, consistently pointing to a market bottom in 2025 before a potential recovery in 2026. <9> In its Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 report, published on January 31, 2024, the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) provided a comprehensive overview of the mineral industry for 2023. The report confirmed that for fixed contracts, the annual average U.S. price for lithium carbonate was $46,000 per ton in 2023. This represented a 32% decrease from the 2022 average price of $68,100 per ton. The price decline was attributed to concerns of a short-term oversupply, the end of China's subsidies for electric vehicle purchases, and weaker than anticipated global sales of electric vehicles. Despite the price drop, worldwide lithium production, excluding the U.S., grew by 23% in 2023 in response to strong demand from the lithium-ion battery market. <10> Controlled Thermal Resources (CTR) held a groundbreaking ceremony on January 26, 2024, for its integrated geothermal power plant and lithium production facility, known as the Hell's Kitchen project, at the Salton Sea in California. [3, 10] This event marked the official start of construction for the Lithium Valley Campus. [2, 3] The first stage of the project is a $1.85 billion development expected to produce 25,000 metric tons of battery-grade lithium hydroxide annually, enough to support the production of approximately 415,000 electric vehicles. [2, 4] The total project has a potential resource capacity to produce 1,100MW of renewable power and around 300,000 metric tonnes of lithium products per year. [5]

This prediction is based on the expectation that demand growth, primarily from the electric vehicle and energy storage sectors, will outpace supply, leading to continued price volatility throughout the year. Other analysts, including those from Goldman Sachs, have similar projections, with estimates of around $11,000 per tonne in 2025. The forecast for price increases comes despite a significant drop in lithium prices over the past couple of years due to a market oversupply. <2> In its first-quarter 2025 report for the period ending March 31, 2025, Lithium Americas detailed significant progress on its Thacker Pass project in Nevada. Key achievements during the quarter included capitalizing $78.2 million in construction and other project-related costs and installing the first modular housing units at the workforce hub in Winnemucca. The company also reported that detailed engineering was over 60% complete as of March 31, 2025, and is expected to surpass 90% by the end of the year. <3> Piedmont Lithium announced that its joint venture, North American Lithium (NAL), produced 43,261 dry metric tons (dmt) of spodumene concentrate in the first quarter of 2025, the period ending March 31, 2025. This production volume represented a 15% decrease from the prior quarter, which was primarily attributed to reduced mill utilization caused by a combination of unplanned weather-related downtime and a scheduled five-day shutdown. Despite the lower output, lithium recovery rates improved to 69% for the quarter and achieved a new monthly record of 72% in March. <4> On March 20, 2025, President Trump signed an executive order titled "Immediate Measures to Increase American Mineral Production." This directive is part of a broader initiative to enhance the domestic production of critical minerals, such as lithium, and lessen U.S. dependence on foreign suppliers. The order mandates several key actions, including expediting the permitting processes for mining projects, prioritizing mineral extraction as a primary use for relevant federal lands, and delegating authority to the Secretary of Defense to use Defense Production Act (DPA) funds for strategic domestic resource projects. <5> On March 11, 2025, Smackover Lithium, a joint venture between Standard Lithium Ltd. and Equinor, announced a partnership with Koch Technology Solutions (KTS) for its South West Arkansas (SWA) project. [2, 5] The announcement confirmed the successful completion of the final DLE derisking step, with an onsite field-pilot plant surpassing key performance criteria, including exceeding the 95% lithium recovery design basis. [3] This milestone allows for the completion of the project's Definitive Feasibility Study and FEED (Front-End Engineering and Design) work, marking a critical step toward the commercialization of the project in Lafayette and Columbia Counties, Arkansas. The project is poised to be the first commercial geothermal lithium extraction plant near the Salton Sea. The lawsuit alleged that Imperial County violated the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) by approving an Environmental Impact Report that inadequately analyzed and mitigated impacts on air quality, hazardous waste, water supply, and failed to properly consult with local tribes. The dismissal of the lawsuit allows the project to move forward. In response to the ruling, the environmental groups filed an appeal on March 7, 2025, stating their intent to continue pushing for stronger environmental protections. <7> In the fourth quarter of 2024, U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods, including lithium-ion batteries, led to an estimated 15% increase in import costs. This development significantly impacted the automotive sector and was projected to potentially slow the growth of the electric vehicle (EV) market by 10%. Concurrently, the tariffs served as an incentive for domestic lithium production, encouraging investments in U.S.-based extraction and processing ventures. <8> In the fourth quarter of 2024, the U.S. lithium market experienced a pivotal and transformative phase, marked by significant strategic shifts aimed at boosting domestic production and lessening reliance on Chinese imports. [2, 3] This realignment was largely driven by geopolitical tensions and the strategic need to secure a resilient supply chain for the rapidly growing electric vehicle (EV) and renewable energy sectors. [2, 3] Key developments included advancements in new mining projects, such as those in Nevada, California, and the discovery of major reserves in Arkansas's Smackover Formation. [3] Concurrently, sustainable mining practices gained traction, particularly through the advancement and scaling up of Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) technologies, which promise to reduce environmental impact and increase efficiency compared to traditional methods. [3, 7] These efforts were supported by federal policies like the Inflation Reduction Act, which encouraged domestic production. [2] <9> Projections from research firm Fastmarkets indicate that the global lithium market is expected to tighten in 2025 after a period of significant oversupply. The firm anticipates the market surplus will shrink to just 10,000 tonnes in 2025 before swinging into a 1,500-tonne deficit in 2026. This shift is influenced by production cuts and robust annual demand growth from the electric vehicle (EV) sector, forecast at 29% for 2024, and the energy storage system (ESS) sector, which is forecast to grow by 25% in 2024 and accelerate to 37% in 2025.

Prediction target period: from 2026-02-26 to 2026-03-13. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Century Lithium released an updated Feasibility Study for its 100%-owned Angel Island Lithium Project (also known as the Clayton Valley Lithium Project) in Esmeralda County, Nevada. The report outlines an after-tax Net Present Value (NPV) of $4.01 billion at an 8% discount rate and an Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 27.4%. These financial estimates are based on a long-term base case price assumption of $24,000 per tonne for battery-grade lithium carbonate. <2> Lithium Americas provided its 2026 capital expenditure guidance of $1.3 billion to $1.6 billion for Phase 1 of the Thacker Pass lithium project in Nevada. The company noted that strengthening lithium market conditions align favorably with the project's anticipated mechanical completion in late 2027. <3> UBS substantially increased its 2026 lithium carbonate price prediction from roughly US$16,500 to US$26,000 per ton, representing a 58% increase from prior forecasts. This significant upward revision is driven by an extensive review of surging global and US demand for electric vehicles and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), with overall global lithium demand expected to double to 3.4 million tons by 2030. As part of these adjustments, the maximum increase in UBS's lithium price forecasts reached up to 74% for lithium concentrate. <4> The United States and Argentina signed a landmark, $130 billion Critical Minerals Deal aimed at redefining the global supply chain. This strategic partnership grants the U.S. priority access to essential Argentine minerals, particularly lithium and copper, enabling Western automakers to meet strict electric vehicle (EV) battery requirements. By establishing minimum prices, the agreement mitigates market volatility for Argentine producers while helping the U.S. diversify its supply chains away from Chinese markets to better support advancing technologies, defense systems, and the global energy transition. <5> On January 22, 2026, Elko, Nevada-based Lithium Corporation issued a press release highlighting strengthened global and U.S. market fundamentals. The company noted that lithium prices officially moved above $20,000 per tonne for the first time since November 2023, bolstered by unexpectedly strong U.S. domestic energy-storage demand and investments in building a domestic North American battery materials supply chain. <6> An industry analysis on U.S. lithium extraction highlighted a structural crisis, noting that global lithium prices have crashed from their 2021-2022 highs to levels well below domestic operating costs. As a result, companies have been forced to pause or slow down numerous mining projects across the United States, with future investments heavily contingent on substantial price recovery or significant government financial support. <7> Benchmark Mineral Intelligence forecasted that lithium carbonate prices are expected to remain between $15,000 and $17,000 USD per ton in 2025. Additionally, the Nevada North Lithium Project, developed by Surge Battery Metals, is emerging as a globally competitive and strategic U.S. supply source crucial for meeting long-term demand and reducing dependence on overseas imports. <8> On January 12, 2026, the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) released data showing its lithium hydroxide futures contracts achieved a record weekly trading volume of 8,296 tonnes in the first full week of 2026. This record reflects surging financial market participation driven by rapidly rising lithium spot prices and an increase in available market liquidity.
